_comment: V-GAT-024 -- a secret digest is computed in-broker and cannot leave package `classify` (06 §4.2). M1-M4 and M10 break the FORMULA (both digests, all three forms, the 0x1f separator, the form labels); M5-M7 widen the SURFACE, which is the only way a digest gets out of the package; M8-M9 put a writer inside it. The surface mutants are the point: every one of them leaves behaviour identical and every existing behavioural test green.

mutants.why: without 0x1f the salted digest is sha256(ns||value), so namespace `team` + secret `a...` and namespace `teama` + secret `...` collide and a hit names the wrong owner
the unsalted digest is the one that catches the cross-namespace copy -- read from namespace A, written into namespace B, which is the exfiltration shape rather than the coincidence shape
a secret that went into a connection string or a webhook URL is URL-encoded, and the gate stops seeing it
`data:` is base64, so the encoded form is what someone actually copies out of a Secret and into a ConfigMap

one exported accessor and every digest is reachable from any package that holds a DigestSet -- the journal writer, the notifier, anything with a logger. Behaviour is unchanged and no behavioural test can see it

edits.find: // Len reports how many digests are in the set, for metrics and tests. Never logs the contents.

mutants.why: same escape by a different door: an exported field needs no method at all, and `%+v` on the struct prints every digest
SecretHit reaches the journal, the chat notification and the audit log; a field that can hold the value is the leak the whole rule exists to prevent, and it leaks on the day someone populates it
06 §4.2 says digests are never logged; a logger in the package that holds them turns that from a property of the code into a promise about call sites

edits.replace:
func init() { log.SetPrefix("classify: ") }

func hashHex(b []byte) string {

mutants.why: no import needed for this one -- `fmt` is already here, and stdout in a pod IS the log
the reason string tells a human HOW the material matched -- raw, base64 or url -- and that is what distinguishes a leak from a legitimate reference
